statusText: Roughly five hours after the U.S. cash open (about 2:29pm ET): the confirmed August UMich consumer sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM) remain digested. Major indices hold a modest, contained pullback from Thursday's record close -- the S&P 500 and Dow both down about 0.2%, the Nasdaq-100 down about 0.4% per the latest midday-into-afternoon reporting -- a day after the S&P 500 first cleared 7,800. NQ futures held within the same confirmed session range as last hour (30,124.25-30,232.00), last quoted around 30,177.50, mid-range and giving back part of an earlier push toward the range high; no failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure has been observed in NQ itself. VIX holds calm near 14.5 (today's range about 14.48-14.65). The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 5bp to roughly 4.69% today, with reporting attributing the move to both the soft retail sales print and a fresh U.S. statement that its naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue "indefinitely" -- a modest incremental escalation in rhetoric, though not yet a confirmed new price-transmission shock into equities. WTI held flat near $81.3 (range $80.77-82.99), while Brent firmed somewhat (quoted from $87.16 up to a reported $88.38, +1.5%) as broader outlets (Washington Post, Al Jazeera) picked up wider coverage today of the previously-flagged Thursday-evening UAE tanker drone attacks in the Strait of Hormuz -- this reads as expanded media pickup of an already-known event plus incremental blockade rhetoric, not a fresh discrete attack. Semiconductors and megacaps were broadly resilient (AMD +3.0% on a well-received bond issuance, NVDA +0.2%, Micron +1.9%, SanDisk +5.6%), conflicting with the modest index-level softness and reinforcing a mixed, non-directional read. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota (25 requests) was already exhausted from earlier runs today; both a live call and one retry returned rate_limit errors, so no Alpha Vantage data was used this run. Most direct financial-data site fetches (Yahoo Finance, TheStreet, Barchart) were also blocked by the network egress proxy, so this run relies entirely on WebSearch snippets, with reasonable cross-source corroboration on the index moves, VIX, yields, oil and the Hormuz coverage, but no single authoritative fresh NQ tick.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail eases slightly to 7% (low) because NQ itself continues to show no persistent one-way structure -- the confirmed session range is unchanged from last hour and the current print sits mid-range, giving back part of an earlier push toward the top rather than extending through it. Stress eases modestly to 40% (still moderate, upper band) as the UMich/Retail Sales surprise is further behind the tape, offset by broader media pickup of the Hormuz tanker attacks and a fresh U.S. blockade-rhetoric headline that keep the geopolitical Stress driver from decaying faster. Confidence eases to 42% (medium-low) from the prior run because Alpha Vantage's free-tier quota was fully exhausted this run (zero successful calls versus two stale-but-successful calls last hour) and most direct financial-data site fetches were blocked, leaving this hour's assessment entirely dependent on WebSearch snippets. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself -- not the standing data misses, the Hormuz coverage/rhetoric on their own, or any single-stock catalyst.
headline: Confirmed UMich miss and already-absorbed Retail Sales drop stay digested as major indices hold a modest, contained 0.2-0.4% pullback into the final trading hours; broader press picked up the known Thursday Hormuz tanker attacks and a fresh U.S. blockade-rhetoric headline today, but VIX (~14.5) stays calm, NQ holds its established range, and semis/megacaps (AMD +3%) stay resilient.
body: At 18:29 UTC, roughly five hours after the U.S. cash open, the confirmed August University of Michigan consumer sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus, down from 55.2 in July) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM vs +0.1% expected) remain fully digested. Major indices hold a modest, contained give-back from Thursday's record close: the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both down about 0.2%, the Nasdaq-100 down about 0.4% per the latest available reporting, a day after the S&P 500 first cleared 7,800. NQ futures held within the same confirmed session range as last hour -- 30,124.25 to 30,232.00 -- with the most recent corroborated quote around 30,177.50, sitting mid-range and giving back part of an earlier push toward the range high; no failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure has been observed in NQ itself, and the last confirmed range has now held stable across multiple consecutive hourly runs. VIX remains calm, near 14.5 (today's reported range about 14.48-14.65), essentially unchanged from the prior run. The 10-year Treasury yield rose roughly 5 basis points to about 4.69% today; CNBC reporting attributed the move to both the soft retail sales print and a fresh U.S. statement that its naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue "indefinitely," a modest incremental escalation in official rhetoric, though not yet a confirmed new price-transmission shock into equities. The 2-year Treasury yield had no fresh confirmed print available this run and is carried forward as stale (last confirmed near 4.20%, dated August 12). Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota (25 requests, shared across today's hourly runs) was already exhausted before this run began: both an initial MARKET_STATUS call and a single retry on TREASURY_YIELD returned rate_limit errors, so per the economical-use instruction no further Alpha Vantage calls were attempted and no Alpha Vantage data was used this run. WTI crude held essentially flat near $81.3 (today's range $80.77-82.99, +0.02%), while Brent firmed somewhat -- quotes ranged from $87.16 (futures, prior close $87.07) up to a separately reported $88.38 spot print (+1.51%) -- as broader outlets including the Washington Post and Al Jazeera expanded coverage today of the previously-flagged Thursday-evening UAE tanker drone attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, with the UAE calling the incident 'piracy.' This reads as wider media pickup of an already-known Thursday-evening event, layered with incremental U.S. blockade rhetoric, rather than a fresh discrete attack or a confirmed new escalation in market transmission; oil has not broken out of its recent range in response. Semiconductors and megacaps were broadly resilient into the afternoon: AMD rose about 3.0% on a well-received investment-grade bond issuance and reassuring long-term growth commentary, NVIDIA was up about 0.2% ahead of its August 26 earnings, Micron gained about 1.9%, and SanDisk added about 5.6% following its Investor Day -- a notably firmer tape than the modest index-level softness, reinforcing a mixed, non-directional cross-asset read rather than a coherent risk-off rotation. In other single-stock news, Reddit extended its gain (up as much as 10-14% intraday) ahead of joining the S&P 500 on August 18, while Globant remained down about 12.6% on disappointing Q2 earnings; neither is an index-level one-way catalyst. Tail eases to 7% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself -- the confirmed NQ range is unchanged and holding for multiple consecutive hours, and the current print sits mid-range rather than showing failed-pullback or repeated-extension behavior. Stress eases modestly to 40% (moderate, still upper band) from 41% last hour: the UMich/Retail Sales surprise is further behind the tape, but broader media pickup of the Hormuz tanker attacks and the fresh blockade-rhetoric headline keep the geopolitical Stress driver from decaying faster, and the Brent/WTI divergence (Brent firmer, WTI flat) is consistent with a regionally-concentrated risk premium rather than broad commodity-market stress. Confidence eases to 42% (medium-low) from 45% last hour because Alpha Vantage's daily quota was fully exhausted this run with zero successful calls (versus two stale-but-successful calls last hour), and most direct financial-data site fetches (Yahoo Finance, TheStreet, Barchart) were again blocked by the network egress proxy, leaving this hour's index-level, NQ-specific, and yield evidence entirely dependent on WebSearch snippets -- with reasonable cross-source corroboration on the index moves, VIX, oil, and the Hormuz coverage, but no single authoritative fresh NQ tick and no fresh confirmed 2-year yield print.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (8-16%) through the trailing 24 hours, easing steadily from Thursday evening's post-CPI/PPI digestion into a stable single-digit floor through Friday's Asian/European session, then holding 7-9% through today's confirmed UMich and Retail Sales misses into the mid-afternoon U.S. session. Stress ran from the upper-30s Thursday evening down to a low of 23% in the early Friday Asian session, then rebuilt steadily through the European morning and into the confirmed UMich print, peaking at 44% before easing modestly and then holding roughly flat around 40-42% as the data digested further without a confirmed equity-market breakdown; the newly confirmed Strait of Hormuz tanker/drone attacks (Thursday evening and again today) add a persistent, if still contained, event-importance driver to the current read.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (2-7%) through the next 24 hours as no confirmed persistent one-way NQ structure is in evidence and no further high-impact U.S. data is scheduled before the Friday close. Stress is projected to resume easing from today's moderate band as the UMich/Retail Sales data and the Hormuz coverage/blockade rhetoric are further digested through the remainder of the U.S. session, dropping toward the low-teens by the ~21:00-22:00 UTC Friday close/CME weekend halt for NQ. From roughly 22:00 UTC Friday through the end of this forecast window (17:00 UTC Saturday), NQ futures are closed for the CME weekend break (reopening Sunday ~22:00 UTC), so Tail and Stress are held near a low weekend baseline reflecting the absence of active price-path evidence and standing weekend headline/gap risk (principally the Hormuz standoff) rather than any newly observed structure. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the low-40s toward the mid-20s as the horizon moves away from this run's evidence and, further out, away from any live trading session at all.
